messages:
ana: Hey folks — noticed a weird discrepancy on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate when we split by model variant. Merged endpoint p50/p95/p99 look fine, but variant A's p99 is much higher than expected. Anyone seen this before?

mike: Could be sampling differences or routing bias. Quick numbers?

ana: Merged (window): p50=40ms, p95=120ms, p99=240ms, sample_count=12,324.
Variant A: p50=35ms, p95=110ms, p99=350ms, sample_count=362.
Variant B: p50=42ms, p95=130ms, p99=230ms, sample_count=11,960.

sarah: With only ~362 samples for A the p99 is noisy. But +350ms vs merged is pretty large. Do we know if A is getting a disproportionate share of fallback/large-prompt traffic?

jordan: Also remember tdigest rollups + reservoir sampling can blow up tails if compression settings are aggressive for small buckets. We compress differently at rollup->daily to save space.

ana: Query I ran in console: ```SELECT quantile(0.99, latency_ms) as p99, count() as sample_count FROM request_latency WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND model_variant='A' AND ts >= now() - interval '1 hour'``` — console UI aggregates with reservoir sampling + tdigest on the backend.

mike: Two angles: (1) sampling/origin bias (routing causing long requests to be routed to A), (2) telemetry aggregation artifacts (tdigest/reservoir).

leo: Can you dump raw samples for that time window? If there's a couple of extreme outliers they'll dominate p99 for small N.

ana: Ran a quick export: ```curl -s 'https://int-metrics/api/samples?endpoint=%2Fv1%2Fgenerate&model_variant=A&start=2026-03-19T10:00:00Z&end=2026-03-19T11:00:00Z' | jq '.samples | length, .samples | map(.latency_ms) | sort'``` returned: length = 362, latencies (sorted tail) = [..., 42, 45, 47, 180, 360]

sarah: There's your culprit — that 360ms outlier pushes p99 up a lot with low N.

jordan: Actionable: (A) annotate dashboard to show sample_count next to each percentile; (B) add a subtle low-sample warning when sample_count < 1000; (C) consider not showing 99th percentile for buckets under a threshold or show CI.

mike: +1 on CI. We could run a bootstrap estimate for p99 and show a confidence interval in the UI when sample_count < 2k. Also show sample_origin tags (route vs fallback) so we can filter out long-running exceptional paths.

ana: Another thought: routing policy for A was recently tweaked — route_weight=0.1 but with overflow_policy=spill_to_A_on_cache_miss. That could bias A toward heavier requests (cache-miss fallbacks).

leo: If we add sample_origin and route_override tags to telemetry, we can surface a breakdown: cache_hit vs cache_miss vs fallback. That will help decide whether those outliers are legitimate for variant A.

jordan: For the tdigest/rollup side: we should ensure the rollup pipeline preserves sample_count and min/max for each rollup shard and avoid compressing extremely small buckets into tight tdigest centroids. It would help to preserve raw tail markers for buckets with N < 1k.

ana: I'll open a console-ux PR to: (1) show sample_count inline, (2) display a low-sample warning badge, (3) offer a toggle to hide p99 when sample_count < threshold.

sarah: I'll file an infra ticket to add sample_origin + route_override to the metrics schema and a short design doc for rollup centroid handling.

mike: I'll prototype a UI for p99 CI (bootstrap) and a small tooltip explaining when percentiles are unstable.

deploy-bot: Deployed: feat/percentile-sample-indicators -> staging (sha: ab12c9d) :shipit:

ana: Thanks all — should we also add a tiny note on the dashboard docs about percentile reliability vs sample_count?

jordan: Yes, docs + tooltip + automated annotation when we detect small N.

ana: Opening tickets now and will ping PRs. Thanks! :thumbsup:
